newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Boeing see battle for Asia-Pacific jet marke.
newsitem.headline: Boeing see battle for Asia-Pacific jet marke.

text.p: Boeing Co Marketing Vice President Bruce Dennis said the Asia Pacific was an "incredible battleground" where the fight is on to win 4,400 new jet orders worth $370 billion, over the next 20 years.

In Hong Kong to present Boeing's Current Market Outlook, Dennis said the world's highest air travel growth will be in the Asia-Pacific region which will enjoy a 6.6 percent per year increase compared to 3.1 percent in the US and 4.4 percent in Europe.

China is expected to be the largest international airliner market with a forecast total of 1,900 worth $124 billion over the next 20 years. So far this year, China has ordered $1.13 billion worth of Boeing aircraft.
"We are seeing very, very high growth rates, it is very robust. It is marvellous what is going on here," Dennis told reporters.
"I think this is going to be a long run growth period because airlines have shown a lot of restraint and there is no sign of the overheated airplane buying spree of the late 80's," he added.
The biggest demand among Asia-Pacific carriers is for the intermediate, twin aisle airliner such as the 777 and Airbus A330 twinjets.

With market fragmentation, Asian airlines are leading the campaign for ultra-long range versions, provisionally called the 777-200X and 777-300X, to open up new city pairings such as Hong Kong-New York, Singapore-Los Angeles and Bangkok-Los Angeles non-stop, Dennis said.
Boeing has already said it is boosting 777 production rate to an unprecedented 40 a month later this year from 22.5 per month in 1996.
Boeing and rivals Airbus broadly agree on the size of the world market for 16,160 airliners worth $1.1 trillion.

But the Boeing executive said because markets are fragmenting and demand for new city to city pairings increases, the two major aircraft manufacturers profoundly disagree on the requirement for a new very large aircraft to succeed the Boeing 747.
Boeing sees a market for 500-plus seaters to be 480 aircraft, while Airbus forecasts a market of 1,200.

"We think there are only 20 airlines such as Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Japan Airlines Co Ltd and Singapore Airlines Ltd which require an ultra-large aircraft which means they would each have to buy 60 aircraft costing more than $200 million each. It does not pass the reality check and that's we decided to postpone pour plans," Dennis said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
